paper.title: Online learning with noisy side observations

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with noisy side observations (weighted observation graphs)
unmapped: Weighted directed feedback graph with edge weights s in [0,1]; side observation c_{t,i} = s*loss + (1-s)*noise
Observation noise zero-mean, independent, bounded by known constant R
Self-loops have weight 1 (own loss observed without corruption)
Bounds depend on effective independence number alpha* = min_eps alpha(G(eps))/eps^2
settings.definition_quote: The learner also observes $G_t$ and the feedback $c_{t,i} = s_{t,(I_t,i)}\cdot \ell_{t,i} + (1-s_{t,(I_t,i)})\cdot \xi_{t,i}$ for every arm $i$ ... We assume that each $\xi_{t,i}$ is zero-mean, satisfies $|\xi_{t,i}|\le R$ for some known constant $R\ge 0$ ... we consider adaptive (or non-oblivious) environments

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with noisy side observations (oblivious graph sequence, tuned thresholds)
unmapped: Weighted directed feedback graph with edge weights in [0,1], noisy side observations with noise bounded by known R
Proof assumes graphs chosen obliviously before the first round
Fixed eta, gamma optimized using knowledge of sum_t alpha(G_t(eps_t))/eps_t^2 and thresholds eps_t
settings.definition_quote: consider an oblivious adversary that chooses the whole sequence of observations graphs deterministically before the first round.

symbols.sum_alpha_eps: sum_t alpha(G_t(eps_t))/eps_t^2, alpha(G_t(eps_t)) independence number of thresholded graph

conditions: graph sequence chosen obliviously (as in proof)

source.label: thm:naive
source.quote: For all $t$, let $\alpha^*_t$ be the effective independence number of $G_t$. Then, there exists a setting of $(\eta_t)$ and $(\gamma_t)$ for which the regret of \expixt is bounded as $R_T = \tOO\pa{(1+R)\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\alpha(G_t(\varepsilon_t))}{\varepsilon_t^2}}}.$

results.notes: Regret defined as max_i E[sum loss_{I_t} - sum loss_i]. Existential tuning; with optimal eps_t gives O~(sqrt(sum alpha*_t)).

symbols.sum_alpha_star: sum_t alpha*_t, sum of effective independence numbers of G_t

source.label: thm:mainTheorem
source.quote: For all $t$, let $\alpha^*_t$ be the effective independence number of $G_t$. Then, setting $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{{\log N}}{{2(1+R+R^2)(N + \sum_{s=1}^{t-1}Q_s)}}}$ and $\gamma_t =R\eta_t$, the regret of \expwix is bounded as $R_T = \tOO\pa{(1+R)\sqrt{N+\sum_{t=1}^T \alpha^*_t}}.$

results.notes: Paper's N is K. Parameter-free w.r.t. alpha* and T.
